mechanisms.description: A small set of cores, commonly the final core, receives disproportionate work or a slower tail path.
mechanisms.name: Concentrated tail or uneven core work

mechanisms.description: Global or PIPE_ALL synchronization inside a repeated stage blocks otherwise independent work.
mechanisms.name: Synchronization is broader or more frequent than dependencies require

mechanisms.description: Overlapping UB/L1/L0 live ranges consume enough capacity to force small tiles, spills, or single buffering.
mechanisms.name: On-chip live ranges constrain tile or pipeline depth

mechanisms.description: Configured buffering does not produce a steady overlap because queue, event, or loop order serializes stages.
mechanisms.name: Copy and compute stages are serialized

mechanisms.description: An intermediate with a local producer and consumer is copied to GM and read back instead of remaining on chip.
mechanisms.name: Intermediate data makes avoidable GM round trips

mechanisms.description: Per-element access, repeated branches, or object/state manipulation consumes material scalar time.
mechanisms.name: Scalar control or elementwise work dominates a hot loop

mechanisms.description: Many small DataCopy operations create high MTE instruction density without approaching bandwidth limits.
mechanisms.name: Small transfers amplify MTE setup cost

mechanisms.description: Concurrent vector operands alias bank geometry through offsets, padding, or stride periodicity.
mechanisms.name: UB layout causes bank or bank-group conflict

mechanisms.description: For a non-tiny workload, task construction or fixed blockDim leaves useful AI cores idle.
mechanisms.name: Available task parallelism is not exposed

mechanisms.description: Required evidence is absent, contradictory, or outside the seeded mechanism vocabulary; this is a first-class non-claim.
mechanisms.name: Evidence does not resolve a supported mechanism

mechanisms.description: Small repeat/count, repeated masks, Cast chains, or missing repeat/stride features reduce useful vector work per call.
mechanisms.name: Vector work is fragmented into inefficient API calls

mechanisms.description: The attainable utilization for the shape is low enough that invasive optimization is not justified by current evidence.
mechanisms.name: Workload cannot amortize fixed overhead

predicates.rule: observed GM bytes materially exceed the algorithmic traffic lower bound
predicates.unknown_when: theoretical traffic or memory counters are unavailable

predicates.rule: MTE ratio is high while achieved bandwidth and useful bytes per MTE instruction are low
predicates.unknown_when: instruction count, bytes, or platform bandwidth is unavailable

predicates.rule: copy and compute intervals are predominantly serialized or contain repeated gaps
predicates.unknown_when: timeline or equivalent overlap counters are unavailable
fewer than two valid per-core samples are available

predicates.rule: scalar ratio and absolute scalar time are material for a non-tiny workload
predicates.unknown_when: scalar pipe counters or stable duration are unavailable

predicates.rule: effective tasks or launched blocks are fewer than available cores
predicates.unknown_when: task count or hardware core count is unavailable

predicates.rule: UB conflict counters exceed calibrated platform thresholds
vector calls are numerous with small repeat/count and low theoretical utilization
predicates.unknown_when: vector instruction or API-level evidence is unavailable

predicates.rule: blockDim is fixed or task construction does not scale with shape and tile count
predicates.unknown_when: host tiling or launch source is unavailable

predicates.rule: a multi-step compute chain copies an intermediate to GM and subsequently copies it back on chip
DataCopy is repeatedly issued in an inner loop with small contiguous payloads
predicates.unknown_when: copy count or valid byte count cannot be derived

predicates.rule: a hot loop performs per-element GetValue/SetValue or scalar arithmetic instead of a vector API
single-buffer queue order or immediate SetFlag/WaitFlag prevents the next stage from being issued early
predicates.unknown_when: queue depth or event ordering is unavailable

predicates.rule: SyncAll, PIPE_ALL barrier, or equivalently broad synchronization executes inside a repeated tile loop
predicates.unknown_when: barrier scope or loop nesting cannot be resolved

predicates.rule: the final core receives a disproportionate tail or executes a substantially slower tail-only path
predicates.unknown_when: per-core assignment or tail path is unavailable

predicates.rule: aligned peak live UB bytes approach capacity and constrain tile size or buffering depth
predicates.unknown_when: buffer lifetimes or target UB capacity is unavailable

predicates.rule: operand offsets or periodic strides map concurrent accesses to the same UB bank or bank group
predicates.unknown_when: layout or bank geometry is unavailable

predicates.rule: work is too small to amortize launch, scalar, and transfer setup overhead
predicates.unknown_when: shape, effective core count, or workload model is unavailable

transformations.applicability: Per-core work is imbalanced and the tail or weighted task assignment is identified as the cause.
capacity_constraints: task metadata and offsets fit existing host/kernel contracts
transformations.name: Distribute tail work across cores
transformations.rollback_spec: restore the original task-to-core assignment and offset calculation
semantic_invariants: every logical element is assigned exactly once
output ordering remains unchanged
tail accesses remain in bounds

transformations.applicability: Repeated vector calls operate on compatible contiguous regions or can use repeat/stride features.
capacity_constraints: batched region fits the selected tile and API repeat limits
contraindications: batch crosses a dependency or non-contiguous boundary
expected_profile_delta: higher useful vector work per instruction
transformations.name: Batch fragmented vector API calls
transformations.rollback_spec: restore the original per-chunk vector calls and masks
semantic_invariants: mask and tail semantics are preserved
broadcast and stride interpretation is unchanged
dtype and rounding mode are unchanged

transformations.applicability: Small DataCopy operations cover adjacent logical data and bandwidth is not already saturated.
capacity_constraints: coalesced transfer and required staging fit on-chip capacity
contraindications: achieved bandwidth is already near platform limit
source regions are not logically contiguous
expected_profile_delta: more useful bytes per MTE instruction
no increase in algorithmic GM bytes
transformations.name: Coalesce adjacent small transfers
transformations.rollback_spec: restore original copy loop, offsets, and tail handling
semantic_invariants: logical output order is unchanged
tail reads and writes remain in bounds
padding cannot enter compute or comparison

transformations.applicability: A non-tiny workload has independent outer/group/head/M/N/S2 work but effective tasks are below available cores.
capacity_constraints: per-task tile and any partial workspace fit platform capacity
contraindications: workload is tiny or overhead limited
split requires an unproven cross-core reduction
transformations.name: Expose more independent tasks with dynamic core selection
transformations.rollback_spec: restore original task construction, blockDim, offsets, and workspace layout
semantic_invariants: tasks partition the logical domain exactly once
partial reductions use the required accumulator precision
dynamic shapes recompute offsets and tails

transformations.applicability: A locally consumed intermediate is written to GM and reloaded while its live range can fit on chip.
capacity_constraints: aligned peak live bytes including the resident intermediate fit the selected memory
main tile and required buffering still fit
contraindications: intermediate must persist across kernels or tasks
residency reduces the main tile enough to negate benefit
expected_profile_delta: lower GM read and write bytes
transformations.name: Keep a producer-consumer intermediate on chip
transformations.rollback_spec: restore the intermediate CopyOut/CopyIn path and original buffer lifetimes
semantic_invariants: producer-consumer order is preserved
dtype and accumulator precision are unchanged
final externally visible output is written exactly once

transformations.applicability: A repeated broad barrier orders independent stages beyond the true producer-consumer dependency.
capacity_constraints: event or workspace slots do not alias while live
transformations.name: Replace broad synchronization with dependency-scoped synchronization
transformations.rollback_spec: restore original barrier and event ordering
semantic_invariants: every consumer waits for its producer
buffer reuse cannot race outstanding work
cross-core visibility requirements remain satisfied

transformations.applicability: Evidence is unresolved, workload-limited, contraindicated, or no candidate clears expected-value and safety thresholds.
transformations.name: NOOP / stop without a patch
transformations.rollback_spec: no rollback is required because no mutation is permitted
semantic_invariants: source tree and executable artifacts are unchanged

transformations.applicability: Conflict counters and layout analysis identify a repeatable UB bank or bank-group collision.
capacity_constraints: new aligned offsets and padding fit UB at peak live range
contraindications: padding causes capacity spill or smaller profitable tile
transformations.name: Alter UB offsets or padding to avoid bank conflicts
transformations.rollback_spec: restore original UB offsets, strides, and allocation size
semantic_invariants: logical indexing ignores physical padding
vector stride remains within API limits
all accesses remain aligned and in bounds

transformations.applicability: A live-range map proves that large on-chip buffers do not overlap semantically.
capacity_constraints: recomputed aligned peak live bytes fit target capacity
queue depth and required double buffers remain valid
contraindications: reuse crosses an asynchronous stage without a proven barrier
expected_profile_delta: larger feasible tile or buffering depth
transformations.name: Reuse on-chip storage across disjoint live ranges
transformations.rollback_spec: restore separate allocations and original lifetime barriers
semantic_invariants: aliased buffers have disjoint live ranges
all outstanding async users complete before reuse
alignment requirements are preserved

transformations.applicability: At least two iterations exist, buffering capacity is available, and timeline evidence shows serial copy/compute stages.
capacity_constraints: all live buffer slots fit UB/L1/L0
loop trip count can reach a steady state
contraindications: loop trip count is below two
transformations.name: Rewrite loop as prolog, steady state, and drain
transformations.rollback_spec: restore original loop, queue depth, and event order
semantic_invariants: stage dependencies are preserved
a slot is not reused before its consumer completes
prolog and drain cover every tile exactly once

transformations.applicability: A hot scalar loop performs elementwise work supported by a target vector API with explicit tail handling.
capacity_constraints: required vector temporaries fit the on-chip budget
contraindications: no semantically equivalent supported vector API exists
workload is tiny and vector setup dominates
transformations.name: Replace scalar element loop with a vector API path
transformations.rollback_spec: restore original scalar loop and element access path
semantic_invariants: dtype, rounding, NaN, and saturation semantics match the original
tail elements outside the logical range cannot affect output
no production GetValue/SetValue fallback is introduced
